findings.what: E10 PORT RULE P3/P4 has a concrete build trap and no mechanical checklist. `kaggle kernels pull -m` returns the AUTHOR's metadata. That metadata can carry is_private=false, enable_internet=true, an id_no and blank "" dataset_sources (private or deleted inputs). P4 says 'change only id and title', so the copy would be pushed PUBLIC with internet ON. An internet-on notebook cannot be submitted to this code competition, and blank sources mean a non-public input that P3 should reject. It would also break the team's private-notebook rule. The rule also does not require the pulled version to be the version that shows the >= 0.956 score, and a later unscored author version can differ. The node-count gate ('within 1% of the author's own log') has no tool, and x138 logs have no single total-nodes line.

Our tested path experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/kernel-metadata.json: is_private true, enable_internet false, no id_no. x138 anchors: BIOHUB_VALIDATOR_ENABLE='0', BIOHUB_REPAIR_DEADLINE_S='27000'. Kaggle CLI 2.2.4. CONTEXT l.2139-2148 (E10 P1-P8).
findings.action: Before any trigger, add P4b to the E10 rule as a mechanical clarification (no new mechanism; within the user's 09:10 conditional yes). After the pull: (a) set id=vitaliineibauer/biohub-exp63-succ-<author> and a title; set is_private=true and enable_internet=false; delete id_no; keep docker_image, machine_shape, enable_gpu and every non-blank source unchanged. (b) P3 FAILS if any source is "" or cannot be listed from our account (`kaggle datasets files <ref>` for each; models via `kaggle models get`). (c) The pulled notebook must be the version whose page shows the >= 0.956 score: compare the version number on the page with the pull, or pull the output of that version (`kaggle kernels output <author>/<slug>`) and check that its log matches the pulled code. A newer unscored version = no port. (d) grep the notebook: BIOHUB_VALIDATOR_ENABLE must be '0'; there must be no PP-sweep selection that scores test stems, no cached CSV or test-derived dataset, and REPAIR_DEADLINE_S must be 27000, else R5 is UNPROVEN (P5). (e) Dummy gate: run tools/dummy_gates.validate_csv on our dummy submission.csv and on the author's output submission.csv of that version. Pass iff it is valid and the per-clip node counts are within 1% (sha256 equality recorded as info). Note in CONTEXT that the pulled metadata is never pushed as-is.

findings.what: The runtime ledger would mis-handle an E10 port. tools/runtime_ledger.py EXP_RULES has no exp63 entry, so the poller's automatic refresh (lb_poll.py calls the ledger without --family) shows exp63 as 'unknown' with no R5(a) evaluation. The module docstring's example is '--family exp63=safetail' (9.5 h deadline). E10 P5 requires the x138 family (7.5 h). A copy-paste of the example would report ADMIT for a port with L in (7.5, 9.5] h, which violates P5/P6 (R5(a) L_hi <= 7.5 h).
